name: Chichen Itza
blurb: Online conversations regarding Chichen Itza highlight visits to the ancient Maya city and its famous archaeological structures in the Yucatán. Visitors frequently discuss historical features like El Castillo and note that climbing the pyramids is no longer permitted.

positive: Impressive architectural features and acoustic effects at the pyramid
Fascinating historical and astronomical significance of the structures
Enjoyable day trips and guided excursions from nearby resort areas
negative: Miserably hot, sunny, and humid weather conditions
Disappointment over no longer being able to climb the pyramids

quotes.text: So this is the coolest thing I've ever seen as a tourist. The Pyramid at Chichen Itza emits a bird call if you clap your hands the base. I don't need the video, I remember the sound so vividly even though I was a kid. It was so impressive.

How bad is it for folks in DC?  On the 4th of July I visited Chichen Itza, on the Yucatan peninsula, in the middle of the jungle.  Miserably hot, full sun, 95 F and humid.  And yet still better than DC's weather that day.

We visited Chichen Itza in Mexico when I got married as I like visiting archaeological sites & they let you go up ALL the pyramids. I took my then young adult children 14 years ago and was disappointed we could no longer do the same as an American was caught pissing at the top of the main pyramid.

We avoided all the crowds along the resort areas but did stop at Chichen itza.  Amazing but overwhelming with all the tourists and vendors after a week of quiet and bird song.
